- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 5–10% below model output.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots downward — cap forecast decline to 1–2% below true low.  
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (±0.3), model overestimates mean reversion — adjust forecast to align with 1–2 day lagged history.  
- When sentiment is positive (e.g., > 0.5) and price is rising, model often over-optimistically forecasts continuation — reduce forecast by 3–5% to avoid overbought bias.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion within 10–15 days after a peak, model tends to underestimate the drop — add 1–2% downward adjustment to forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven volatility — multiply sentiment magnitude by 0.7–0.8 to adjust forecast volatility.
